cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). It's preached that Christ has been raised from the dead. But some of them are saying something that doesn't fit with that at ALL.

cards.question: What are some people in Corinth saying that clashes with Christ being raised?

answers.text: There is no resurrection of the dead
Paul is not a real apostle

cards.question: Some in Corinth say there is no resurrection of the dead. Paul says that even then, Christ could still have been raised.

cards.text: So Paul follows that idea all the way out, like pulling one loose thread on a sweater, friend. If Christ has not been raised, two things become worthless right along with it.

cards.question: Paul says if Christ has not been raised, the apostles' ___ is worthless, and so is the Corinthians' ___.

cards.text: Now it gets personal for Paul. He and the others have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead.

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, what does Paul say that would make him and the others?

cards.text: Then Paul circles back to his main point: if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised. And he spells out more of what that would mean for the Corinthians.

cards.question: If Christ has not been raised, Paul tells the Corinthians their faith is ___.
And if Christ wasn't raised, where does Paul say that leaves the Corinthians?

cards.text: Then Paul thinks about the believers who have already died. He calls them those who have fallen asleep in Christ.

cards.question: If Christ wasn't raised, Paul says those who have fallen asleep in Christ are simply resting safely.

cards.text: Then Paul zooms way out, and he includes himself. What if our hope in Christ is only for this life?

cards.question: What does Paul say about believers if their hope in Christ is for this life alone?

answers.text: They should be pitied more than anyone
They should be envied more than anyone
They should be feared more than anyone

cards.text: Then Paul flips it: "But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep." SOMEBODY get this man a microphone!

cards.question: Paul calls the risen Christ the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep. What does that picture point to?

answers.text: He is the first of many to be raised
He is the only one ever to be raised
He was the first person ever to die

cards.text: Paul explains how it all works. Death came through a man.

cards.question: Since death came through a man, Paul says the resurrection of the dead comes through the angels.
Paul says in ___ all die, and in ___ all will be made alive.

cards.text: But it doesn't all happen at once: each in his own turn. Like take-a-number tickets at the DMV, everybody gets called, just not all at the same time.

cards.question: Christ goes first as the firstfruits. Who does Paul say comes next?

answers.text: Those who belong to Him at His coming
Everyone on earth the very next day

cards.text: Then the end will come. Christ destroys all dominion, authority and power, and hands over the kingdom to God the Father.

cards.question: Paul says Christ must reign until something happens. Until what?

answers.text: Until all His enemies are under His feet
Until the temple is rebuilt in Jerusalem
Until the last apostle has died

cards.question: Paul says the last enemy to be destroyed is ___.

cards.text: Paul quotes Scripture (Psalm 8:6): "God has put everything under His feet." Then he points out the obvious: everything doesn't include God, the One who put everything under Him.

cards.question: Paul says that when all things are subjected to the Son, the Son Himself will be made subject to God, so that God may be all in all.

cards.text: Paul comes at it from another angle. He points to people who are baptized for the dead.

cards.question: Paul asks why people are baptized for the dead if the dead are not raised at all.

cards.text: Then Paul turns it on himself and the others. Why would they put themselves in danger every hour?

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians he faces death every ___.

cards.text: Me? I held my breath every time that junk drawer opened, scared it was cleanout day, and Paul faces death EVERY SINGLE DAY. Then he asks, "If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain?"

cards.question: If the dead are not raised, what way of living does Paul say might as well take over?

answers.text: Live it up since tomorrow we die
Work hard since the end is near
Stay quiet since no one is listening

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians the company they keep has no effect on their character.

cards.text: Then Paul gives them a wake-up call. Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning.

cards.question: Why does Paul tell the Corinthians to sober up and stop sinning?

answers.text: Some of them are ignorant of God
Some of them are leaving the church
Some of them are too proud to pray

cards.text: Paul tells them, "I say this to your shame." But don't close the cookie box yet, friend, because he's not finished teaching on this.

findings.problem: Card 3 asks whether Christ could still have been raised if there is no resurrection of the dead (v13). Card 1 already says the Corinthians' claim 'doesn't fit with that at ALL', and card 2's question says the claim 'clashes with Christ being raised'. Together they give away card 3's answer before the baker reaches it.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The DMV joke says 'everybody gets called'. Verse 23 limits the next turn to 'those who belong to Him' at His coming, so the joke muddies the fact. It also makes card 7's wrong answer 'Everyone on earth the very next day' look more right.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it.

findings.problem: Adam first appears here, as the answer to a fill in the blank. No card says who he is (the first man), even after the answer is revealed.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain retellings with no Papa Dorin voice or humor: stop 1 cards 1, 6, 8, 11 and 13; stop 2 cards 3, 8 and 11; stop 3 cards 1, 3 and 8. Stop 1 has only the sweater line. The walkthrough reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: **But he is FUNNY.** Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Many story cards are stripped down to a bare restatement of the verse, with little of Papa Dorin's voice, for example stop 2 card 3 ('Paul explains how it all works. Death came through a man.') and stop 3 card 1.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
